prompt: Implement BrightnessAdjuster.adjust, which adds delta to every red, green and blue channel of every pixel and clamps each result into 0..255.
explanation: Each channel only holds eight bits, so an unclamped 200 + 60 would overflow into the neighbouring channel when the pixel is repacked and produce a wildly wrong colour. Clamping with a small helper that pushes anything below 0 up to 0 and anything above 255 down to 255 keeps every channel legal for both brightening and darkening. The pattern is the standard one for pixel maths: unpack with shifts and 0xFF masks, transform each channel independently, repack with shifts and |.
hints: Extract the three channels separately -- (rgb >> 16) & 0xFF, (rgb >> 8) & 0xFF and rgb & 0xFF -- then add delta to each.
Write one small private helper that takes an int and returns 0 if it is negative, 255 if it is over 255, and the value otherwise; call it on all three channels.
Repack the clamped channels as (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b and setRGB that into the OUTPUT image so src stays untouched.
